mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly housing starts (HOUST) above 2000.0 units signals strengthening residential construction, which precedes higher consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when HOUST exceeds 2000.0 units, or the rank correlation between HOUST and SPX 20-day returns is below 0.05 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, it signals active monetary tightening that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and SPX 20-day returns exceeds 0.05 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.8%) and rise in housing starts (HOUST > 2150.0 units) indicates robust labor market conditions fueling consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE < 4.8% and HOUST > 2150.0 units, or the interaction term (UNRATE * HOUST) has a rank correlation below 0.03 with SPX 5-day returns over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production contractions (INDPRO < 105.0), manufacturing slowdowns reduce corporate profitability expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and SPX 60-day returns exceeds 0.05 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL > 198.0) indicates accelerating inflation, which typically triggers interest rate hikes and reduces equity attractiveness, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 198.0, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and SPX 5-day returns is below -0.05 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate exceeds 5.5%, it signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending power and corporate revenue growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when UNRATE > 5.5%, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and SPX 60-day returns exceeds 0.05 over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) indicates monetary tightening during economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and INDPRO < 105.0, or the interaction term (FEDFUNDS * INDPRO) has a rank correlation below -0.03 with SPX 20-day returns over a 5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During strong GDP growth (GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% annualized), economic expansion boosts corporate earnings and investor confidence, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when GDPC1 growth rate > 2.0% annualized, or the rank correlation between GDPC1 growth rate and SPX 5-day returns is below 0.05 over a 5-year rolling window.
